_comment: Everything this skill says that is not a number and not a lesson prompt.
Script only — recording happens separately and is not part of a build phase.
`speaksPrompts: false` from the first commit. This skill starts at eight and
a child of eight can read; reading a word problem aloud to them takes the
reading out of the question. Division learned that after recording 74 clips
What it does say is what it says *back* to a child: the reactions, which come
from the common pack and name no subject, and the refusals below — the
sentence an engine gives when it will not take an answer yet. Those fire
while a child is looking at a strip rather than at text, and apparatus that
refuses a move in silence reads as broken rather than as restrained.
These are copied from the engines' own refusal tables, not written by hand.
The first version of this file was written from the plan before the engines
existed, and every one of its four lines turned out to be a sentence nothing
in the skill ever said. `fractions.voice.test.ts` now checks both directions.
The speaker button stays, unrecorded, on the live TTS path: a child who can
do the fractions but is stuck on the reading should have a way through.
phrases: Mark the strip into those pieces first, then count how many there are.
Now shade the second one down the grid. The answer is where they cross.
Put the marker on the line first.
Shade more of them — count how many the question asked for.
Shade the first fraction across the grid before you answer.
That has gone past it. Come back one step.
That is an equal fraction, but it can still be made simpler.
That is too many. Take one off.
The pieces are different sizes. Make them match before you count.
There are still enough loose ones to make another whole.
There is still a whole one to break up.
These pieces are different sizes. Cut them to match before you count.
